title: XYZ bullet formula
text: Write bullets as: accomplished X, measured by Y, by doing Z. Lead with the outcome, then the method.

title: Quantify impact
text: Quantify impact with percentages, revenue, latency, cost savings, users served or time saved. Never invent numbers; use scale words if no metric exists.

title: Strong action verbs
text: Open each bullet with a strong past-tense action verb such as Architected, Led, Reduced, Shipped, Automated. Avoid 'responsible for' and 'worked on'.

title: ATS keyword alignment
text: Mirror exact keywords and tool names from the job description where the candidate genuinely has the experience. ATS parsers match literal terms.

title: ATS-safe formatting
text: Use standard headings (Summary, Experience, Projects, Education, Skills), a single column, no tables or images, and consistent date formats.

title: Concise bullets
text: Keep bullets to one or two lines, roughly 12 to 28 words. Use three to six bullets per role, with the most for the most recent role.

title: Tailored summary
text: The summary should name the target role, years of experience, two or three signature strengths and one headline achievement.

title: Truthfulness
text: Never fabricate employers, titles, dates, metrics or skills. Rephrase and reorder real experience; flag gaps instead of hiding them.

title: Placeholders for missing metrics
text: When an achievement clearly had an outcome but the resume gives no number, suggest a bracketed placeholder such as [reduced X by __%] for the candidate to fill in, instead of inventing a figure or dropping the impact.

title: Scope and scale words
text: If no metric exists, show scope instead: team size, number of users or customers, data volume, request rate, budget or number of services owned.

title: Order by relevance
text: Put the experience and bullets most relevant to the target job first. Recent, relevant work deserves the most space; compress older or unrelated roles.

title: Avoid empty buzzwords
text: Cut unsupported adjectives such as results-driven, passionate, synergy or rockstar. Demonstrate qualities through concrete outcomes instead.

title: Skills section
text: Group skills by category (Languages, Frameworks, Cloud, Data, Tools), list only skills actually used, and spell them the way the job description does.

title: Consistent tense
text: Use past tense for previous roles and present tense for the current role. Keep date formats consistent throughout.

title: Spell out acronyms once
text: Write important acronyms both ways once, for example Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) or Continuous Integration (CI/CD), so ATS keyword matching works for either form.

title: One idea per bullet
text: Each bullet should carry one achievement. Split bullets that join unrelated work with 'and also'.

title: No personal pronouns
text: Drop I, me and my. Start bullets with the verb.

title: Impact over duties
text: Describe what changed because of the work, not the job description. 'Reduced onboarding time 40%' beats 'Responsible for onboarding'.

title: Resume length
text: Keep the resume to one page with under about 10 years of experience and two pages at most otherwise.

title: Links that help
text: Include GitHub, portfolio or publication links when they show relevant work; make sure they are current.

title: Show soft skills through results
text: Demonstrate leadership, communication and collaboration through bullets (mentoring, cross-team launches, stakeholder decisions) rather than listing them as skills.

title: Certifications
text: List certifications that the job asks for or that prove a required skill (for example AWS, CKA, Security+), with the year obtained.

title: New graduates and juniors
text: Lead with education, internships, projects and relevant coursework. Projects should name the tech stack, your role and a concrete result or link.

title: Projects section
text: For each project give one line of what it does, the stack, and an outcome such as users, stars, accuracy or a demo link. Personal and academic projects count.

title: Internships count
text: Treat internships like jobs: action verb, what you built, the tools, and the result or scale. Mention code review or production deployment if it happened.

title: Senior and lead roles
text: Emphasize scope and influence: architecture decisions, cross-team initiatives, mentoring, hiring, incident leadership and business outcomes, not only individual tasks.

title: Leadership without a title
text: Show leadership through owned initiatives, mentoring, leading incident response, writing design docs or driving adoption of a practice.

title: Career switchers
text: Bridge the gap in the summary, lead with transferable achievements and relevant projects, and describe past roles in terms of skills the new role needs.

title: Employment gaps
text: Do not hide or disguise gaps. Keep dates honest; if useful, list relevant study, projects or caregiving briefly.

title: Recent tools first
text: Prefer current, in-demand tools the job lists. Drop outdated technologies unless the job asks for them.
